changelog: - **The run row names the current phase.** A document can name the phases of its run, each with its first and last step, and while the run is under way the run row shows the phase the current step belongs to beside the step count. The coffee roasting batch names seven: Charge, Drying, Browning, Development, Drop, Cooling and Discharge. The step count keeps its place and no control moves; the tooltip gives the name with its steps. Where a name has no room, every phase of the document is shown as a small button that opens the name and its steps when pressed or focused, never as a cut name. On a phone the name and its steps are a line above the run controls, there only while a phase is under way. A screen reader hears the phase with the step when it changes. A phase is the author's guide, not a result: nothing is computed from it. In a project revision the phases are part of what is reviewed: they are one line of the difference list, applying a proposal takes them with its timetables, choosing changes can take or keep them, and one Undo takes the graph and the phases back together. Before an Apply that would leave the phase names and the timetables on different sides, the review says that the current phase shown may then differ from the real process. The review's summary also names a difference in the timetables, the step length or the kinds, which used to read as no change. An earlier version of the app opens such a document without the phase names and runs the same, and it reports a project revision that has phases as written by a newer version. There is no editor for phases yet; they come with a Template or a file. The coffee batch's phase names follow all 18 languages.
